newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson to be national champion -Chirac.
newsitem.headline: Thomson to be national champion -Chirac.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Saturday that defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF's destiny was to be France's national champion in electronics and play a central role in the restructuring of Europe's defence industry.

"Thomson-CSF's vocation is to be the national electronics pole that France needs. It must play a central role in the European restructuring of our defence industries," he said at the Thomson-CSF pavilion at the official opening of the 42nd Paris air show at Le Bourget. He was accompanied by Thomson-CSF chairman Marcel Roulet.

Chirac was reiterating comments made in February last year when he launched the privatisation of Thomson-CSF as part of a French defence industry consolidation. The state owns 58 percent of Thomson-CSF.
The previous conservative government had received bids for the defence company from conglomerate Lagardere and telecommunications and engineering group Alcatel Alsthom .
But the arrival at the beginning of June of a Socialist government hostile to state sell-offs has thrown up huge doubts over the future of Thomson-CSF.

The sale of Thomson-CSF is viewed as a key step in reorganising French and European defence activities and executives hope next Saturday's keynote speech by Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin will clarify the government's plans.

Chirac later said while visiting the defence minstry's pavilion that "a considerable effort has been made in the last two years to modernise the defence industry, reduce costs and promote exports. This effort must continue."
